body: Replacing the legacy frozen dashboard with a modern SPA console requires a seamless single-binary distribution strategy for on-prem and local developers, while allowing containerized deployment for SaaS. This item defines the asset embedding pipeline.
_note: Full authoring of context, epic, and ACs

brief.problem: Product Forge web console and dashboard assets must be securely bundled and served directly by the platform binary without shipping exposed web source files or running Node.js at runtime.
brief.what_adds: Next-Gen Web Console Packaging Specification: embed pre-compiled SPA distribution assets into Go platform server binary.

label: PF Backlog 688
risks: Binary size increase from embedded assets mitigated via asset compression and selective asset chunking.
title: Next-Gen Web Console Packaging Specification: embed pre-compiled SPA distribution assets into Go platform server binary
summary: Define and implement the build-time pipeline that embeds compiled SPA static web assets into the Go server binary via embed.FS, with support for decoupled container hosting in SaaS.
approach: Use vite build to produce static dist/, embed via go:embed in Go server binary, and catalog console asset bundle in EAP manifest.
rollback: Serve web console from external static directory via configuration flag.
objective: Define and automate the web console compilation pipeline to produce an embedded static SPA distribution served directly by Go core server.

api_impact.reason: Packaging, deployment, and verification CLI/core capability; no dedicated HTTP routes required

verification: Build tests asserting binary asset embedding, HTTP 200 SPA route resolution, and zero node_modules in output packages.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Web console build pipeline compiles SPA frontend into optimized HTML/JS/CSS assets with content hashing and integrity checks.
AC-2: Go platform server embeds compiled frontend assets via go:embed and serves them with HTTP cache headers and gzip compression.
AC-3: Shipped customer packages contain zero Node.js runtime dependencies or raw TypeScript/JSX source files.
